This earnings plateau stems primarily from elevated Kazakh central bank interest rates pushing the cost of funding up 150 basis points year-over-year to 14.5%, compressing fintech spreads. Simultaneously, investors view the cross-border expansion into Turkey via Hepsiburada and the acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. (rebranded as Hepsi Bank) as a capital-intensive distraction that dilutes consolidated margins and reduces near-term dividend payout capacity.

1. What the Market is Pricing In

Mr. Market is pricing in a pronounced emerging-market and regulatory discount for Kaspi.kz, focusing on the recent divergence between top-line expansion (15% year-over-year revenue growth) and stagnant bottom-line net income. This earnings plateau stems primarily from elevated Kazakh central bank interest rates pushing the cost of funding up 150 basis points year-over-year to 14.5%, compressing fintech spreads. Simultaneously, investors view the cross-border expansion into Turkey via Hepsiburada and the acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. (rebranded as Hepsi Bank) as a capital-intensive distraction that dilutes consolidated margins and reduces near-term dividend payout capacity.

Furthermore, the stock's valuation multiple of 13.6x P/OE (and ~8.5x reported P/E) reflects persistent frontier-market governance anxieties, residual skepticism from historical short-seller campaigns alleging secondary sanctions risk, and broader geopolitical concerns regarding Central Asia. By valuing Kaspi at a steep discount to global platform monopolies, the market treats current domestic cash flows as mature and vulnerable, assuming that elevated funding costs and Turkish integration friction will permanently impair owner returns.

2. Why It Might Be Right (The Skeptic Gate)

Merchant pushback against bundled advertising and logistics fees forces the 3P e-commerce take-rate down from 16.1% to 12.0%, while Payments TPV declines 15% to $22.4B as competition intensifies.
4
Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation
High fixed costs in logistics networks, banking infrastructure, and elevated deposit expenses trigger severe operational deleverage. Blended owner cash margins collapse from 16.2% to 10.0%, shrinking Year 3 Owner Earnings to $750.0M total, or $3.95 per share on an impaired revenue base of $7,500.0M.
5
Downside Risk Valuation Floor
Applying a trough frontier multiple of 6.0x P/OE to degraded earnings of $3.95 per share ($23.70) and adding depleted ending net cash of $1.50 per share yields a Downside Floor Target of $25.20 per share.

3. How Things Are Going Now

Kaspi's operational performance demonstrates the durability of its closed-loop ecosystem, generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $9,200.0M ($2.3B quarterly, +15% YoY) with a solid 58.1% gross margin. Capital allocation and strategic expansion remain highly disciplined. Management increased the Q2 2026 dividend by 18% year-over-year to ₸1,000 per ADS, underscoring strong internal cash generation. Simultaneously, Kaspi rolled out its proprietary AI shopping assistant 'Kasper' to rapid consumer adoption (driving tailored product recommendations) and completed the acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. in Turkey, establishing Hepsi Bank to unlock fintech cross-selling across Hepsiburada's merchant and consumer base.

4
Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings

market_pricing_in:
At the current quote of $96.07, Mr. Market is pricing Kaspi.kz at a deeply discounted valuation multiple of 8.2x P/OE and 7.9x EV/OE, implying an owner cash yield of 12.1%. This steep valuation discount reflects intense macro and geopolitical skepticism rather than fundamental business deterioration. Market participants are heavily fixated on the lingering overhang from short-seller allegations regarding regional sanctions compliance, alongside sovereign risk concerns inherent to operating primarily in Kazakhstan. Furthermore, recent regulatory actions—including increased commercial banking reserve requirements, higher corporate tax burdens, and potential anti-monopoly mandates that could force open Kaspi's proprietary QR-code payment network—have spurred fears that the company's take rates and margin structure have peaked.

This pricing disconnect presents a classic value asymmetry. The market is treating Kaspi's earnings as cyclical or vulnerable to imminent structural decay, completely discounting its net cash balance sheet of $4.51 per share, 44.0% return on invested capital, and rapid double-digit expansion across marketplace and payments. Rather than valuing Kaspi as an entrenched national digital ecosystem with sticky multi-product network effects, Mr. Market is treating the franchise like an unhedged emerging market lender whose profitability will be permanently compressed by regulatory mandates and regional contagion.
